brief:
Today, 5 November, is Push B at the New York gym. Nothing new has been logged since Legs A on 3 November, and no Push B is logged for 4 November, so this review repeats yesterday’s and tonight’s numbers are the same ones. If you did train on 4 November and the log has not reached the repo, these numbers are for a night you already did. Once it lands, the app sets this review aside and runs its standing rules until the next review.

The program does not change today. It stays at version 7. No new night means no new reason to move anything, and one pass has only just given most lifts a number on these machines.

Tonight, Push B, 20 sets, in pounds. Shoulder press: 50 lb dumbbells for 10, four sets. Machine chest press: 135 for 10, three sets, logged as you go. Dumbbell lateral raise: 15 for 15, three sets. High-to-low crossover: 29 for 15, two sets. Reverse pec deck: 90 for 13, three sets; this is its last chance on Push B, and if it is skipped with no note it comes off on the morning of 6 November. If the machine was taken or the night ran short, a note saying so keeps it. Rope pushdown: 47.5 for 12, three sets. Last slot: 50 for 12, two sets, under the name you typed, Overhead db press. One word in the note settles it: “triceps” if it was one dumbbell held overhead in both hands, “press” if it was two dumbbells pressed. If it is pressed, stop where the set stops and log it; that would also mean extra shoulder work on a triceps slot and six direct triceps sets rather than eight. With no word, the slot keeps these numbers. Cue: control the pec deck and keep your shoulders down on the raises; the chest press sets only count toward 150 if they are logged live.

Next is Pull B, written the morning after tonight’s log lands. The plan going in: chest-supported row 50 for 9, four sets; close pulldown 112.5 for 10, then 127.5 for 10, 10; straight-arm 37.5 for 12, three sets; shrug 80 for 16, four sets; incline curl 30 for 10, 10; reverse curl 32.5 for 12, three sets; face pulls 32.5 for 12, two sets.

The dated decisions each moved one day because Push B did not log: pec deck 6 November, fourth shrug set 7 November, abs and calves 8 November. The counting rule and your “Why four sets?” on the seated row stay on 9 November.

One question is open again, because it now touches numbers. The log carries no gym name before 22 September, so I cannot tell whether New York’s machines are the ones you used in August. Tonight’s cards come from New York nights either way. If they are the same machines, the seated row (105 for 10s against 12s on 28 August), pec deck (90 for 13, 12, 12 against 15s on 27 August) and leg extension (150 for 10s against 13s on 20 August) are below August at the same weight, this block is winning that back, and the leg extension’s next card stays at 150 rather than dropping to 142.5. Without an answer, I keep treating New York as its own baseline. One word in tonight’s note settles it: “same” or “different”.

Three things I still cannot tell from the log. First, the crunch: both leg-night crunch cards read Plank at this gym until the name is blanked, and I do not know whether you chose the plank or ran out of time. You objected to seconds on an ab lift on 30 July, so a timed hold stays off the card unless you ask for it. Second, your logs from 28 October to 3 November are stamped Meso 3, weeks 5 and 6, while the calendar puts all six nights in week 1 of the restarted block. Those stamps match a phase locked to Meso 3 by the phase tag at the top of the app; I cannot see that setting from here. It changes no numbers today, but if it is locked on 25 November, the deload will not start by itself. “Automatic (by date)” is the option that clears it. Third, no bodyweight has been logged since 23 August (207 lb), and a morning weigh-in would anchor the block.

A reading note on the muscle review: every “a week done” figure counts half credit from compound lifts, so compare it with the number on paper, not the direct-set count beside it.

Conditioning: the build block allows 2 to 3 low-intensity sessions of 20 to 30 minutes a week, and the log has no conditioning file since 21 July. Nothing extra is asked of you tonight.

block.why: Nothing new has been logged since yesterday’s review, so this review repeats it with the dates moved: the log’s last night is still Legs A on 3 November, and no Push B is logged for 4 November. Today is the second day of week 2 of 4 in the restarted block, which builds to 24 November; deload runs 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, and the show is 116 days away. Legs A on 3 November finished the first full pass on one set of machines, the reason the block was restarted: six nights in seven days (28, 29, 30, 31 October, 2 and 3 November), 108 of the 121 sets the current program asks for, counting what you did in place of a slot. The shortfall is mostly two nights: Legs B on 30 October (14 of 20) and Push B on 31 October (17 of 20). So the block is on course, with two limits. The first four lifts of Push A on 28 October and the 30 October leg press were typed in from memory, so those are starting numbers until they are logged live. And the log carries no gym name before 22 September, so I cannot tell whether New York’s machines are the August ones; if they are, several lifts sit under August at the same weight (seated row 105 for 10s against 12s on 28 August, pec deck 90 for 13, 12, 12 against 15s on 27 August), and this block is winning back August rather than setting a first baseline. The nights logged live show first repeats going up (leg curl, leg press, deadlift). Nothing changes in the program today. Rotating lifts after one pass would throw away the baseline before it can show anything, and the dossier’s stalled list mostly compares machines across gyms or against August nights that carry no gym. The leg-night order also stays: Legs A ends on the crunch and Legs B ends on the calf press, so if the last slot is what gets cut, calves still get Legs A and abs still get Legs B. The four-week averages below read lower than current training because they include this week, with only Pull A and Legs A so far, and the week of 19 October, with no chest, triceps or quads. Tonight’s Push B numbers are the ones written on 3 and 4 November, unchanged, because no push lift has been logged since 31 October. The first three dates below moved one day because Push B did not log on 4 November; the 9 November date did not move. Dated: Push B pec deck 6 November, fourth shrug set 7 November, abs and calves 8 November, the counting rule and the fourth row set 9 November. The muscle lines below give direct sets where they help, but every “a week done” figure counts half credit from compound lifts, so it compares with the number on paper, not the direct count. Next boundary is the deload on 25 November; the prep block is written at the assessment from what these four weeks log.

Tonight, do whichever it was at 50 for 12, two sets, and write one word in the note (“triceps” or “press”); the slot then becomes the lift you name, and the card already carries the name you typed.
